Someone Bought a Mercedes-Maybach, Drove 500 Miles and Took It Back to the Dealer
10 photos
Photo: BenzsandBowties | YouTube
Someone paid a fortune to take this Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 home and returned it after just 532 miles. With a V8 under the hood and ultra-luxury features, it obviously isn't a car for anyone. Yet, what in the world could have possibly gone wrong to make the owner trade it in that soon?
Pre-owned at just 532 miles or 856 kilometers. This is what this dealership is selling. It is an ultra-low-mileage 2026 Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 finished in MANUFAKTUR Exclusive Silver Metallic, which is a $9,900 option on top of the starting price of $224,900, excluding destination charges and before checking any option boxes.
The hood is finished in Obsidian Black Metallic, displaying the "Monogram" pattern and 307 Maybach "MM" logos directly onto it. The hood is split in two by a sleek chrome fin running down the middle, leading from the standing Mercedes star logo right to the bottom of the windshield.
At the time of the sale, it was the only Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 in this color combo imported to the United States, says Doug Horner, General Sales Manager at Mercedes-Benz of North Olmsted. He reveals that one of their VIP customers bought the high-end Maybach convertible and five months later, decided to return it.
Photo: BenzsandBowties | YouTube The luxury roadster comes with the MANUFAKTUR Crystal White Nappa leather interior, which is the sole standard cabin choice for the Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series . The white leather covers just about everything on board, from the seats, center console, dashboard, and A-pillars to the entire door panels. High-pile, plush white mats featuring the Maybach logo cover the floor. The roadster rides on 21-inch Maybach multi-spoke forged wheels.
This is the car that has recently been unloaded in the dealer’s yard with only 532 miles on the clock. This means that the original owner did not have much of a chance to enjoy the performance of the model.
The Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 comes wth an AMG-derived powertrain, refined specifically for a smoother, ultra-luxury grand touring experience, typical of the Maybach models. The 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8.
The V8 pushes out 577 horsepower (585 metric horsepower) and 590 pound-feet (800 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make the Maybach roadster rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.0 seconds, run the quarter mile in 11.8 seconds with a trap speed of 121 mph (195 kph), on its way to a top speed of 161 mph (260 kph).
Photo: BenzsandBowties | YouTube Doug Horner doesn’t reveal what sort of car the former owner of the Mercedes-Maybach. Now, he is left with an ultra-low-mileage, five-month-old ultra-luxury car to sell. The Maybach still has three years and seven months, or nearly 49,500 miles (79,663 kilometers), left on the warranty, which basically makes it still a brand-new car. Now, Doug will have to set the asking price.
